text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- The Serbian government adopted measures for major construction projects -- trans-Yugoslav highways and water resources.
- The New York round table on (Serbian province) Kosovo is an attempt to internationalise the issue of Kosovo and break up Yugoslavia, says Politika commentary.
- U.S. calls on Serbs in Eastern Slavonia in Croatia to take part in elections.
- U.N. transitional administration in Eastern Slavonia, Croatia, accepted demands of the Serb regional parliament and extended the deadline for registration of voters.
- Belgrade's rail company Zeleznicko Transportno Preduzece Beograd signed an 80 million French francs deal with French producer of wheels and axles for rail road cars Valdunes.
- Sugar beet sowing in Serbia is almost finished. Sugar producers estimate beet area of 87,000 hectares, well below the government plan of 100,000 ha.

- French commercial attache to Yugoslavia Andre Lambert visited Kragujevac and warned that Yugoslavia "could face problems joining the European Union if Zastava car plant decides to cooperate with South Korea's Hyundai Motor Company".

- The managing board of the Zastava Group dismissed managing director of Zastava car plant Miodrag Bogdanovic from his post because of "catastrophic business results and failure to meet 1996 production target despite the financial help received from the Serbian government".
NASA BORBA
- Vojvodina coalition says bill on ownership transformation in Serbia is a deceit.
- If the European Union approves exports preferentials to Yugoslavia, real effects can be expected next year.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- State owes more than a billion dinars to pharmaceutical industry and that is the reason for shortage of medicines and low utilisation of production capacities.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin pensioners' association in its public appeal to state officials ask for reasonable and honest compromise on current political dispute between the republic's president Momir Bulatovic and prime minister Milo Djukanovic.
- Montenegrin students' organisation call on all involved in the political conflict to resolve their disputes in a democratic way.
- Montenegrin electric power company adopted plan for construction of new power plants in the republic.
- Podgorica office of Danish Refugee Council will provide loans to refugees for income generating projects.
MONITOR
- The current political turmoil in the republic could lead to dictatorship, says editorial of Esad Kocan.
- Strike in Radio Cetinje.
- Rebroadcast of Serbian television attack on Djukanovic on TV Montenegro was ordered by Predrag Bulatovic, head of the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists MPs club.
- Montenegrin home page on Internet opens Montenegro without taboos.
- Manifesto of 50 university professors for Democratic and Free Montenegro is a sign that university is waking up, says prof Nebojsa Vucinic in an interview.
